39	 * home medication list, inpatient medications, allergies, vital signs, and copies of lab results the
40	 * author reviewed.

42	 * Read these before mapping:
43	 *
44	 * - **Every document re-lists the home medications and allergies.** Each list is a snapshot taken when
45	 *   that document was signed, with that document's status for each drug. Five documents in one stay
46	 *   mean five copies of the same drugs. For the hospital's final word on outpatient medications, use the
47	 *   most recent `discharge_summary` of the encounter.
48	 * - **Lab results are copies.** Riverside does not publish lab results as items of their own. A result
49	 *   appears inside whichever documents reviewed it, so the same result can appear in several items. The
50	 *   `accession` plus test code identifies one result across documents.
51	 * - **Lab values are text**, exactly as the lab displayed them: `"182"`, `"7.21"`, `"<0.01"`.
52	 * - **Payload times are UTC** (`Z`). Riverside is in America/Chicago (UTC-6 standard, UTC-5 daylight
53	 *   time). The clinical date of an evening visit is the local date, which can be a day earlier than the
54	 *   UTC date. Times written in the narrative are local wall-clock times.
55	 * - **No allergy/intolerance distinction.** Everything on the hospital's allergy list is an `allergy`
56	 *   entry, including side effects such as cough.
57	 *
58	 * Envelope conventions: `effective` is the time the document is about (ED arrival for an ED note, time
59	 * of examination for an H&P, progress note or consult, inpatient admission time for a discharge
60	 * summary, with `effective_end` = discharge time). `author` is the signing clinician. A signed addendum
61	 * or correction is a new item that `supersedes` the original and restates the whole document.
62	 */

64	/** One entry in a Riverside document payload. Discriminated by `type`. */

66	  | Encounter
67	  | Diagnosis
68	  | History
69	  | Allergy
70	  | HomeMed

72	  | Vitals

77	/**
78	 * The encounter and document context. Exactly one per item, conventionally under the key `enc`.
79	 */

81	  type: 'encounter';
82	
83	  /**
84	   * Riverside encounter number. One number covers the whole hospital stay, from ED arrival to
85	   * discharge: the ED note, H&P, progress notes, consults and discharge summary of one stay share it.
86	   */
87	  encounter_id: string;
88	
89	  /**
90	   * Which kind of document this item is.
91	   * - 'ed_note': emergency department provider note.
92	   * - 'hp': admission history and physical, written by the admitting physician.
93	   * - 'progress_note': daily inpatient note.
94	   * - 'consult': note from a specialty service asked to see the patient.
95	   * - 'discharge_summary': written at discharge; covers the whole stay. Its home medication list is
96	   *   the discharge instructions.
97	   */
98	  document_kind: 'ed_note' | 'hp' | 'progress_note' | 'consult' | 'discharge_summary';
99	
100	  /**
101	   * Encounter class at the time the document was signed.
102	   * - 'emergency': the patient was in the ED and not yet admitted.
103	   * - 'inpatient': admitted (including step-down and ICU).
104	   * A stay that starts in the ED changes class from 'emergency' to 'inpatient' at admission; earlier
105	   * documents keep the class they were signed with.
106	   */
107	  class: 'emergency' | 'inpatient';
108	
109	  /** Clinical service of the author, free text as configured at Riverside, e.g. "Emergency Medicine", "Hospital Medicine", "Endocrinology". */
110	  service: string;
111	
112	  /** ED arrival time, UTC. Present on every document of a stay that began in the ED. */

114	
115	  /** Inpatient admission order time, UTC. Absent while the patient is still in the ED. */
116	  admitted?: string;

123	   * - 'admitted': ED patient admitted to Riverside (ED notes only).
124	   * - 'home': discharged home without services.
125	   * - 'home_with_services': discharged home with home health.

127	   * - 'left_against_advice': left before the care team discharged them.

129	   */

453	 * Consumer views: the rows a patient-facing chart application shows for one patient's record at one

458	 * including superseded and retracted items) and a local date `asOf` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), and returns

462	 * Rules shared by every view:
463	 *
464	 * - **As-of.** An item counts when its `recorded` time is on or before the end of `asOf` (23:59:59.999 local
465	 *   time). Among those, an item does not count if a counting item supersedes it (directly or through a chain:
466	 *   if C supersedes B and B supersedes A, A is replaced too) or retracts it. A superseding or retracting item

479	 *   other organizations and without correcting the source. Rows come from structured payload entries; the
480	 *   narrative may help interpret an entry, but is never the only basis for a row.
481	 * - **Evidence.** Every row lists the items (and, where the payload has them, entry ids) it rests on; at least

## Admission history and physical

**Reason for admission:** euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis.
